messages.task:
You are a financial analysis assistant.  The user will ask questions that can be answered through careful reading of the following scenario and by invoking the available tools.  Think step-by-step, decide which tool to call, observe its result, and continue until you are confident you have the final numeric answer.  When you are done, reply with ONLY that final answer as an unformatted integer.

Scenario (background information – no further data is available beyond what is written here):
9.
Junior subordinated debt securities payable in accordance with the provisions of the junior subordinated debt securities which were issued on March 29, 2004, Holdings elected to redeem the $329,897 thousand of 6.2% junior subordinated debt securities outstanding on May 24, 2013.  As a result of the early redemption, the company incurred pre-tax expense of $7,282 thousand related to the immediate amortisation of the remaining capitalised issuance costs on the trust preferred securities.
Holdings considered the mechanisms and obligations relating to the trust preferred securities, taken together, constituted a full and unconditional guarantee by Holdings of Capital Trust II’s payment obligations with respect to their trust preferred securities.
10.
Reinsurance and trust agreements – certain subsidiaries of Group have established trust agreements, which effectively use the company’s investments as collateral, as security for assumed losses payable to certain non-affiliated ceding companies.  At December 31, 2015, the total amount on deposit in trust accounts was $454,384 thousand.
On April 24, 2014, the company entered into two collateralised reinsurance agreements with Kilimanjaro Re Limited (“Kilimanjaro”), a Bermuda-based special-purpose reinsurer, to provide the company with catastrophe reinsurance coverage.  These agreements are multi-year reinsurance contracts which cover specified named-storm and earthquake events.  The first agreement provides up to $250,000 thousand of reinsurance coverage from named storms in specified states of the southeastern United States.  The second agreement provides up to $200,000 thousand of reinsurance coverage from named storms in specified states of the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic and Northeast regions of the United States and Puerto Rico as well as reinsurance coverage from earthquakes in specified states of the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic, Northeast and West regions of the United States, Puerto Rico and British Columbia.
On November 18, 2014, the company entered into a collateralised reinsurance agreement with Kilimanjaro Re to provide the company with catastrophe reinsurance coverage.  This agreement is a multi-year reinsurance contract which covers specified earthquake events.  The agreement provides up to $500,000 thousand of reinsurance coverage from earthquakes in the United States, Puerto Rico and Canada.
On December 1, 2015, the company entered into two collateralised reinsurance agreements with Kilimanjaro Re to provide the company with catastrophe reinsurance coverage.  These agreements are multi-year reinsurance contracts which cover named-storm and earthquake events.  The first agreement provides up to $300,000 thousand of reinsurance coverage from named storms and earthquakes in the United States, Puerto Rico and Canada.  The second agreement provides up to $325,000 thousand of reinsurance coverage from named storms and earthquakes in the United States, Puerto Rico and Canada.
Kilimanjaro has financed the various property-catastrophe reinsurance coverage by issuing catastrophe bonds to unrelated, external investors:
• On April 24, 2014, Kilimanjaro issued $450,000 thousand of notes ("Series 2014-1 notes").
• On November 18, 2014, Kilimanjaro issued $500,000 thousand of notes ("Series 2014-2 notes").
• On December 1, 2015, Kilimanjaro issued $625,000 thousand of notes ("Series 2015-1 notes").
The proceeds from these issuances are held in reinsurance trust throughout the duration of the applicable reinsurance agreements and invested solely in U.S. government money-market funds rated at least "AAAm" by Standard & Poor’s.

Available tools (call them exactly as named):
• fetch_issuer_id(issuer_name) – Get the internal numeric ID for a given issuer name.
• fetch_instrument_id(instrument_type) – Get the internal numeric ID for an instrument type such as "notes".
• list_issuance_amounts(issuer_id, instrument_id, start_year, end_year) – Returns a list of issuance amounts (in THOUSANDS of US$) matching all filters.
• aggregate_amounts(amounts) – Return the sum of a list of integers.
• list_all_issuers() – List every issuer present in the database (exploratory).
• list_instruments_for_issuer(issuer_id) – List instrument types used by the given issuer (exploratory).
• thousand_to_absolute(amount_thousand) – Convert a value expressed in thousands to absolute dollars (not required here).

Question you must answer:
What is the total value (in thousands of US dollars) of notes issued by Kilimanjaro in 2014 and 2015?

Think carefully, use the tools when necessary, and respond with the final integer only.
